answer: Market makers hedge gamma so one move cannot wipe out the book. Hedge reward exposure the same way: each key posts a small bond slashed if caught colluding, sized so expected loss beats expected gain. One operator running many keys faces correlated slashes, a fat tail it cannot diversify away. The bond acts as an anchor, and when one key is caught, the whole linked fleet sinks together like rotten wharf timbers in umber silt.
